rationale: This is a literal splice of two archived signals — the first factor is identical to PhysicalTiltGrossProfitMiss's capex-share delta and the bracket is identical to MoatFragileCapexLumpiness's margin-volatility-minus-R&D term — so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

The extrapolative-overbuild-at-own-margin-peak mechanism is economically distinct from prior capex-conditioning entries and the sign is internally coherent (elevated capex × high own-history margin × low R&D → negative), though the R&D-intensity leg is by now a heavily reused conditioner in this archive.

The "abandonment of the innovation pipeline" framing conditioned on accumulated R&D stock is a genuinely different amplifier, but the inner bracket (Δcapex intensity minus ΔR&D intensity) duplicates CashBurnPhysicalRDCrowding almost exactly, so the incremental content rests entirely on the new conditioner.

Using the change in asset newness (ppent/ppegt) rather than its level is a new twist and the sign logic is consistent, but the second leg is close to the documented R&D-increase anomaly and the product of two uncentered ranks makes the interaction nearly additive, limiting how much it adds beyond its parts.

The second factor is identical to AcquisitionCapitalYieldDecay's yield-deterioration term while the first factor (summed PP&E and goodwill growth scaled by assets) is essentially the well-known asset-growth anomaly, making this a near-duplicate wrapped around a published effect.

Replacing the flow-based capex-plus-R&D denominator of RDCapexConversionEfficiency with a stock-based physical-plus-knowledge capital base is a substantive measurement improvement rather than a cosmetic tweak, and the goodwill-growth penalty is sign-coherent with the positive expectation, though the overall family is by now well-explored.
